key_insight: Humidity reshapes FAPbI₃ phase-transition pathways through competing water uptake by a layered metastable intermediate and the photo-inactive δ phase.
engineering_relevance: Understanding moisture-dependent transitions could guide humidity control during perovskite film fabrication and protection against degradation during solar-cell operation.
method: Large-scale atomistic simulations using an ab initio machine-learned potential.
Identification of a water-affine layered intermediate along the Burgers transition pathway.
Analysis of competing water uptake and its influence on transition kinetics.
evidence_signal: Simulations reproduce the experimentally observed rise in the δ-to-α transition temperature with increased humidity; the abstract reports no quantitative accuracy metrics.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish how these atomistic mechanisms translate to device-scale efficiency or operational lifetime.
paper_title: Humidity-modulated Ostwald Step Rule in $\rm FAPbI_3$ Martensitic Transitions
